body:
## Problem

Replay support checks often reduced known Vulkan feature, extension, property, or input constraints to “not supported.” Missing or failed dependencies could also obscure why downstream pipelines were never created.

## What changes

Adds caller-owned support details to the existing feature-filter interface and carries known identifiers, required/available values, and raw unknown IDs into bounded worker diagnostics. Compute, graphics, ray tracing, and static-object checks retain their existing support decisions.

Retains scalar source dependency identities through parsing and scheduling, links blocked consumers to missing or failed modules/parents, and keeps originating failures separate from unattempted consumers. Missing common-cache inputs, parse errors, allocation failures, and driver creation failures remain distinct.

Adds assertion-bearing support, dependency, compatibility, and real worker/controller pipe fixtures, plus private-protocol and verification documentation and an Unreleased changelog entry.

## Why this matters

Users can identify a concrete compatibility boundary or failed prerequisite without treating each blocked pipeline as another compiler fault.

## Why this approach

Value outputs preserve the existing bool callers, while lexical scalar dependency capture avoids retaining parser objects or changing the public StateCreator virtual interface. Bounded examples and independent attempt-scoped counts keep diagnostic retention finite. The private worker protocol carries facts independently of human log verbosity.

## Verification and limits

Reviewed head: `f49ad7ad99fbe33d858e5e0168fe56a3ef3ac8e4`.

- Independent unit checker: full Linux Debug/Release × exceptions OFF/ON, with CLI/layer/SPIR-V validation enabled and runtime-layer testing disabled: **274/274 tests in each configuration**.
- Focused ASan+UBSan: **31/31**, with actual instrumentation verified; six concurrency cases passed three times each; both compiled isolated mutations failed the intended M19 assertions and the strict verifier passed.
- Separate final checker: **145/145 decisive tests in both Debug/OFF and Release/ON**, six concurrency cases repeated three times, and two additional compatibility checks passed after validating the unchanged candidate-bound builds.
- An earlier implementation Release run failed one inherited timeout native-status assertion (273/274). The unchanged full retry, all four fresh independent matrices, and 20 focused timeout repeats passed. The original failure remains recorded; a signal/exit race is a source hypothesis, and the original native status is unknown.

[Independent unit evidence](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/harness-artifacts/runs/issue-19/issue19-20261110/reports/checker-unit-3.json) and [separate final evidence](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/harness-artifacts/runs/issue-19/issue19-20261110/reports/checker-final-1.json) retain commands, statuses and all 14 case mappings.

Native Windows verification was explicitly waived and remains unverified. CPU fixtures do not establish GPU, Steam, driver-cache, or persistence behavior; compatibility checks provide source/invocation evidence rather than a general prebuilt binary ABI guarantee.

## Task references

Closes https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/19

Shared requirements: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/8
